data.name: Models.Subtitle
data.value: What is evicted when a game starts. Only loopback addresses; each server is unloaded by its own API.

data.name: Models.Commands.Note
data.value: For MLink, llama-swap, WSL, Docker and anything else: programs run with no window, exit code 0 = done. Check runs only the check command.

data.name: Plan.Kill
data.value: {0}: stop {1} ({2} GB), start it again with the same command after the game

data.name: Games.Subtitle
data.value: Steam and Epic libraries are found by themselves. A running game turns game mode on; Not a game moves it to the exclusions.

data.name: Games.Excluded.Note
data.value: Apps from game libraries that are not games. Crash handlers and redistributable installers inside game folders are ignored too.

data.name: Journal.Subtitle
data.value: One line per game: what was evicted, what the guard caught and how long the restore took. Kept for 90 days.

data.name: Settings.Grace.Note
data.value: How long no game process must run before models come back. Covers a game restart and launcher hand-offs.

data.name: Settings.Margin.Note
data.value: Restore waits until free VRAM ≥ evicted + margin.

data.name: Settings.WaitVram.Note
data.value: After that, models come back anyway with a warning.

data.name: Settings.Guard.Note
data.value: During a game: a model loaded again is evicted again and written to the journal.

data.name: Settings.KillAnyway
data.value: Stop llama-server even if I can't start it again

data.name: Settings.KillAnyway.Note
data.value: Off by default: without a readable command line the server is left running.

data.name: Exit.Message
data.value:
Models are evicted.
Yes: bring them back now and exit. No: exit now, they come back at the next start. Cancel: keep running.

data.value: How it's unloaded: keep_alive 0 through its API; back with the same context size

data.name: Method.Comfy
data.value: How it's unloaded: POST /free; ComfyUI loads its models again on the next request

data.name: Method.LmStudio
data.value: How it's unloaded: REST API, unload by instance, load back with the same settings; lms unload --all if the server is off

data.name: Guard.Restarted
data.value: llama-server on :{0} started again during the game, {1} min after it was unloaded (started by {2}). Another program brings it back on its own; it is left alone now. For MLink use "Use MLink's commands" on the Models page.

data.name: Guard.MLinkBack
data.value: MLink's model is running again during the game: a model was chosen in MLink's tray, or MLink was started again (that ends the hold). Left alone: it's your choice; Pause in VRAM Bouncer if you want the model during a game.

data.name: MLink.Message
data.value: Its llama-server on :8080 is started again by MLink's watchdog, so stopping it does not free VRAM for long. MLink's own commands keep the model off for the whole game and bring the same model back.

data.name: MLink.Notify
data.value: MLink found: its model should be unloaded by MLink's commands. Click to open Models and turn them on.
